subject: summary.gm.prcomp and plot.gm.prcomp functions missing from 3.3.1?

messages.author: 1326f1b016745db2
messages.subject: summary.gm.prcomp and plot.gm.prcomp functions missing from 3.3.1?
parts:
Hi there,

I recently updated to geomorph 3.3.1 (and RRPP 0.6.1). Maybe I am doing something silly, but I am not seeing the functions summary.gm.prcomp and plot.gm.prcomp that are described in the help documentation.

I am trying to store the proportion variance and cumulative variance to use for making plots. Previously, I did this by assigning the summary to a variable, eg:

PCA <- gm.prcomp(gpa$coords)
PCA_sum <- as.data.frame(summary(PCA))

Now I'm unable to assign the summary to a data frame. From reading the help pages, I have the impression this information is available with the summary.gm.prcomp function, but am I doing something wrong that I can't access this information?

Thanks very much!
Elena

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] summary.gm.prcomp and plot.gm.prcomp functions missing from 3.3.1?
parts:
Elena,

plot() and summary() are generic support functions that will work directly on gm.prcomp class objects. To use them, do, e.g.:

mypca <- gmprcomp(gpa$coords))

summary(mypca)

plot(mypca)

Please see the help file of the function for details on the analytical and plotting options included. The corresponding vignette might also be useful, you can reach it with: vignette("geomorph.PCA")

As for the proportion of variance explained by each component, you can easily calculate that through the squared eigenvalues of the components, i.e.:

mypca$sdev^2 / sum(mypca$sdev^2)

Hope this helps

Antigoni

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] summary.gm.prcomp and plot.gm.prcomp functions missing from 3.3.1?
parts:
Elena,

If you install the latest RRPP and geomorph from Github, you should be able to assign the summary as an object, but as.data.frame() will not work because the summary is a list.  There are two objects in the list, $PC.summary and $Ancestors.summary, the latter of which will be NULL if a phylogeny was not used.  Both should be data frames, already.

summary.gm.prcomp now does quite a few different things, depending on whether components are aligned to principal axes or phylogenetic signal, and whether GLS transformations are performed, so the summaries are a bit more diverse.  However, missing the option to print them to an object was inadvertent.  It’s fixed on Github versions and will be available on the next CRAN release, down the line.

Cheers!
Mike
